Hi Søren — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, followed by proposed next steps. Attachment: redwood-dpa-sccs-summary.pdf, eu-processing-architecture-v1.png.

1) EU-only processing: yes — we support EU-only deployments in two modes that meet this requirement: 
   - Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) hosted in our EU regions — compute, persistent storage, and backups are kept in-region.
   - Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — customer-managed networking and storage inside their EU environment.

2) SCCs & Schrems II: Redwood executes the EU SCCs as part of our DPA for customers selecting EU-only processing. We also provide a set of documented supplementary technical measures (encryption at-rest/in-transit, regional KMS, strict subprocessors list, logging controls). The attached PDF summarizes what we ship by default and optional controls.

3) BYOK / KMS: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (major cloud providers and bring-your-own-key flows) for Dedicated and Private modes. Keys can be provisioned in EU regions.

4) Logs & backups: for EU-only deployments, access logs and backups are configured to remain in the EU. We can provide an operational runbook that lists retention windows and data paths.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal tech Q&A with Marcus (infra) to confirm logging/backups and exact KMS flows — 30min.
- Legal redline DPA sent by Kimberly — we'll provide a DocuSign link for execution.
- Workshop to review supplementary measures and subprocessors (we can provide the current list live).

Can we schedule the tech call on Tue/Wed next week? I'll include Marcus and Kimberly on the invite.

Best,

Subject: Re: Questions on EU-only processing + SCCs (technical clarifications)

Hi all — adding some technical detail for the tech Q&A and for procurement. Short bullets: 

- Compute & Storage: For Dedicated EU-only, all compute (inference/runtime) and persistent storage live in the selected EU region (currently eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 options).
- Backups: Snapshot backups are encrypted and stored in-region; we can restrict cross-region replication.
- Logs: Access and request logs can be configured to be retained in-region. We do keep aggregated telemetry for platform health in our control plane; however for EU-only Dedicated customers we offer an option to limit telemetry export and retain logs on customer-owned storage or in-region buckets.
- KMS/BYOK: Customer-managed keys supported. If using BYOK, telemetry and backups are encrypted under the customer key and Redwood cannot decrypt without customer approval (we do have operational procedures for recovery that would require an explicit approval flow).
- Caches & ephemeral data: KV caches and runtime context are memory-resident and do not persist to global stores. We can provide a design note showing cache lifecycle.
- Subprocessors: the core infra team uses a small set of subprocessors (cloud provider infra, monitoring provider, log storage). We'll provide the up-to-date list; subprocessors operating outside the EU can be avoided for EU-only Dedicated depending on customer needs.

Happy to walk through network diagrams on the call.

— Marcus
